proposed_relationship: Combining cancer vaccines with small-molecule inhibitors of IDO may enhance T-cell function in the tumor microenvironment.
mechanism: The mechanism involves the inhibition of IDO, which degrades tryptophan and suppresses T-cell function, thereby allowing activated T-cells from cancer vaccines to effectively target tumors. This is because tumors upregulate IDO as an immune-evasion mechanism, and small-molecule inhibitors of IDO can counteract this effect. By blocking IDO, the tryptophan levels in the tumor microenvironment may increase, potentially enhancing T-cell activity.
constraint_released: The use of IDO inhibitors releases the constraint of T-cell suppression in the tumor microenvironment, allowing cancer vaccines to be more effective.
predicted_quantitative_outcome: 20% increase in T-cell activation with combined therapy compared to vaccine alone
